interest: This file provides valuable historical insight into Japan's diplomatic, cultural, and economic outreach toward Latin America in late 1938, against the backdrop of the Second Sino-Japanese War and growing Pacific tensions. It demonstrates how economic diplomacy—including Japanese efforts to secure raw cotton, export manufactured textiles, and negotiate commercial treaties—was conducted in tandem with cultural exchanges such as lecture tours and the founding of bilateral cultural societies. Furthermore, the documents illuminate Peru's delicate foreign policy balancing act, highlighting the Peruvian government's domestic anxiety over publicized negotiations with Japan and its successful resistance to Japanese overtures regarding immigration liberalization.
overview: This file covers records from the U.S. State Department dating from September to December 1938 regarding diplomatic, cultural, and economic relations between Japan and Peru. Centered on the visit of the Peruvian Economic and Cultural Mission and the subsequent arrival of cultural envoy Dr. José de la Riva-Agüero, the file comprises cross-reference sheets indexing communications from Lima and Tokyo as well as an excerpt from a Tokyo Embassy periodic political report. The records document the Peruvian mission's seven-week tour across industrial and cultural centers in Japan, Korea, and Manchuria, detailing informal talks concerning reciprocal cotton trade, mineral and fisheries development, and a proposed commercial treaty, while noting Peru's successful avoidance of Japanese proposals on immigration. The documents also describe the mission of former Peruvian Prime Minister Riva-Agüero to deliver lectures and assist in the founding of a Japan-Peruvian Cultural Society.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a telegram regarding the Peruvian Foreign Minister's reaction to press reports of official talks during the Peruvian mission's visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes Telegram No. 462 sent on September 23, 1938, by U.S. representative Louis G. Dreyfus, Jr. in Lima, cross-filed under decimal file 823.628/6. It reports on the visit of the Peruvian Economic and Cultural Mission to Japan. The Peruvian Minister for Foreign Affairs stated that he believed the mission was organized purely for cultural purposes and expressed annoyance at press reports indicating that the delegates were conducting discussions on official matters with Japanese authorities.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Telegram No. 462 from Dreyfus (Lima) on Peruvian Mission to Japan

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a Tokyo despatch concerning the Peruvian Economic and Cultural Mission's visit and the arrival of cultural envoy José de la Riva-Agüero.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes Despatch No. 3521 dated December 20, 1938, from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo, filed under 894.00 P.R./132. It summarizes the seven-week stay of the Peruvian Economic and Cultural Mission in Japan, noting that delegates were lavishly entertained but lacked authority to enter into binding commitments. It also references the arrival of former Peruvian Prime Minister Dr. José de la Riva-Agüero as a cultural envoy to assist in establishing a Japan-Peruvian Cultural Society.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 3521 from Grew (Tokyo) on Peruvian Mission and Cultural Envoy

subfiles.about: Extract from an embassy political report reviewing the Peruvian mission's tour and economic discussions in Japan, as well as the arrival of cultural envoy Dr. José de la Riva-Agüero.
subfiles.summary: This section of a periodic political report from the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo details the seven-week visit of the Peruvian Economic and Cultural Mission across Japan, Korea, and Manchuria from September to November 2, 1938. Although the mission lacked authority to make binding agreements, it engaged in discussions with Japanese industrial and financial leaders, focusing on Peruvian raw cotton exports, Japanese textile sales, and a prospective commercial treaty, while successfully evading Japanese proposals to ease immigration restrictions into Peru. On October 5, resolutions were agreed upon to recommend enhanced bilateral banking, shipping, mining, and fishing cooperation. The report further notes the arrival on November 29 of former Peruvian Prime Minister Dr. José de la Riva-Agüero to deliver lectures and participate in the founding of a Japan-Peruvian Cultural Society.
subfiles.title: Section of Tokyo Embassy Political Report on Peruvian Economic and Cultural Mission and Cultural Envoy
